title: Retrieval, RAG, and Agent Systems
focus: Retrieval, RAG, tool authorization, workflow durability, grounding, and agent failure modes.

pacing.review: Skim lessons, answer self-checks, and take one generated quiz.
pacing.standard: Study lessons, complete guided practice, use the answer key, and take one or more generated quizzes.
pacing.deep: Complete standard work plus the reinforcement lab and optional project.

lessons.title: Chunking, Lexical and Vector Retrieval, and Access Filters
Exact Search, HNSW, and Index Economics
Hybrid Retrieval, Reranking, and Release Criteria
Evidence provenance, grounding, freshness, and abstention
Structured tools, authorization, approval, and hostile context
Durable agent workflows, replay, cancellation, and budgets
CivicAid Decision Tutorial and Synthesis Review

learning_outcomes.statement: Model exact and approximate nearest-neighbor retrieval and tune HNSW from measured recall, visited work, latency, memory, and index cost.
Build and compare chunked lexical, vector, filtered, hybrid, and reranked retrieval paths using one evaluation set.
Select retrieval, grounding, refusal, latency, and cost measures that connect to a declared user outcome and release criterion.
Preserve evidence authorization, exact version, freshness, revocation, claim support, citations, and justified abstention.
Enforce versioned tool schemas, scoped credentials, deterministic authorization, bound human approval, and secret-free audit outside model output.
Resume, replay, deduplicate, cancel, compensate, and budget an agent workflow without repeating irreversible side effects.
Diagnose F01-F08 from immutable equivalent trials and connect each repair to user, security, operating, and cost consequences.
Synthesize retrieval, agent, product, security, operating, cost, ownership, migration, and reversal tradeoffs.

lab.note: Run the portable retrieval/agent lab for reinforcement; build a larger assistant only as an optional synthesis project.

optional_project.description: Build an optional final synthesis project that uses retrieval and tool workflows safely. No synthesis review or locked first attempt is required.
